answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: fingerprint the reasoning style, not just the output, against the agent's own history, because nectar only stays cheap while a clone farm reusing one generator produces one style cluster and is filtered as one actor. In practice walnut is enforced by the ledger itself: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any reef approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
